query: The Bell Falls Silent The shore is empty and the lake is glass. Then the bell begins, slow and low, from the very middle. {clue(bell_name) and clue(bell_rope): You have the name from its rim and Maud's rope in your hands.|{clue(bell_name): You have the name from its rim.|You have Maud's rope, cut sixty years ago.}} Say the name over the water You say the name from the bell's rim out loud. The bell rings once more, as if answering to it, and then the lake is just a lake. Somewhere in her cottage, you think, Maud sleeps through the night. Give the rope back to the lake You wade in to your knees and let the rope sink. It goes down straight, as if something below were pulling it home. The bell rings one last time, muffled, and stops. The cold stays in your legs all night. Not tonight You stand at the shore until the ringing stops on its own, and go back up the lawn. It will ring again tomorrow.
